text:
The equation can be rewritten as  

\[
(y^2-36)(y^2-4)=44^{2^{2025}},\qquad y=x+10 .
\]

Let \(z=y^2\). Then  

\[
z^2-40z+144=44^{2^{2025}} \Longrightarrow 
z^2-40z+(144-44^{2^{2025}})=0 .
\]

Solving this quadratic for \(z\):

\[
z = 20 \pm \sqrt{44^{2^{2025}}+256}.
\]

Because \(44^{2^{2025}}\) is astronomically large,  

\[
20-\sqrt{44^{2^{2025}}+256}<0,
\]

so the corresponding \(y^2\) is negative and gives no real \(y\).  
The only admissible value is  

\[
y^2 = 20 + \sqrt{44^{2^{2025}}+256}>0,
\]

yielding two real solutions  

\[
y = \pm\sqrt{20 + \sqrt{44^{2^{2025}}+256}}.
\]

Returning to \(x = y-10\),

\[
x_1 = \sqrt{20 + \sqrt{44^{2^{2025}}+256}} - 10,\qquad
x_2 = -\sqrt{20 + \sqrt{44^{2^{2025}}+256}} - 10.
\]

The sum of the real roots is  

\[
x_1 + x_2 = -20.
\]

Thus the proposed answer \(0\) is incorrect.  

VERDICT: REJECT
